messages:
anne_support: Heads-up — ACME (customer) filing: multiple client reports of 5xx/long tails since ~08:30 UTC. They say requests are getting routed to na-west even though they expect na-east. sample req IDs: req_9a3f, req_9a40, req_9a41.
acme_infra_jordan: Confirmed. Saw 503 + 3500ms P99 on our end. We see response header `x-serving-region: na-west` and `x-fallback-reason: queue_threshold` for the failed requests.
anne_support: Customer also notes billing spike tied to retries. Sending them repro steps now, pinging oncall.
ryan_oncall: I'm on it. Can you paste a full response header from one of the failed attempts?
acme_infra_jordan: Here's minimal headers we captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-serving-region: na-west
x-fallback-reason: queue_depth_exceeded
x-request-id: req_9a3f
x-retry-after: 1
```
ryan_oncall: Looks like the request got auto-diverted. Checking routing logs and queue metrics for na-east.
devon_sre: FYI, we had a rollout yesterday that lowered the divert threshold from 1200 -> 800 for a short A/B. Might be correlated. Pulling queue depth graphs now.
maya_prodeng: That experiment was supposed to reduce cold queueing during low-load models, but it could cause more frequent diversion under bursts.
ryan_oncall: Metrics: na-east queue depth spiked to 950 at 08:29 UTC, then to 1025 at 08:30 — triggered divert rule. na-west accepted overflow and saw higher latency. Link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/queues/region-queue?orgId=1&var-region=na-east (internal)
anne_support: Customer wants repro steps we can give them to validate routing.
ryan_oncall: Ask them to include `X-Region-Hint: na-east` in a simple curl to check. Example:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Region-Hint: na-east" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
acme_infra_jordan: We ran that curl and still saw na-west for ~30% of requests during the spike window. We also saw `x-fallback-reason: capacity_surge`.
devon_sre: Looking at the routing service logs — snippet:
```
[08:30:12] route_decision: customer=acme team_id=789 route=na-west reason=overflow_policy match=queue_depth>800
[08:30:12] route_debug: candidate_pool=na-east queue_depth=1025 active_inflight=320
```
ryan_oncall: Repro steps for eng: reproduce locally with a short burst script (100 concurrent requests over 10s) against na-east with small token budget. Script: `heyload --concurrency 100 --qps 0 --duration 10 --header "X-Region-Hint: na-east"`
maya_prodeng: Short-term mitigation options: 1) rollback experiment (restore threshold to 1200), 2) temporarily pin ACME to na-east (route override), 3) increase autoscale buffer for na-east.
anne_support: Customer prefers pin for now to avoid billing/retry churn. Asking for ETA.
devon_sre: I'll apply a pin for acme (route override) and rollback the threshold experiment in next 5–10m. Applying pin now.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 — region overflow divert affecting ACME. Priority: P2. Owner: devon_sre.
devon_sre: Pin applied: route override for team_id=789 -> na-east. Confirmed 200 responses for next 50 sampled requests, `x-serving-region: na-east`.
acme_infra_jordan: Confirmed — successful responses and P99 back to normal (~120ms). Billing spike stopped on our side. Thanks. :relieved:
ryan_oncall: Rolling back threshold experiment in traffic-config, will monitor.
devon_sre: Rolled back. Re-run burst test; na-east queue peak settled at 700. No further auto-diverts observed in the test window.
maya_prodeng: Follow-up: we'll schedule a postmortem and include a change to the experiment gating (only apply to low-traffic customers), and add an alert if queue depth crosses 900 for >60s.
anne_support: Please capture repro script + sample logs for the support ticket.
acme_infra_jordan: Uploaded logs + the curl we used to the ticket. Thanks team.
ryan_oncall: Closing loop here — mitigation applied and customer verified. Leaving incident open for postmortem tracking.
anne_support: Marking customer ticket as "mitigated" and will notify ACME once postmortem doc is ready.
devon_sre: Note for postmortem: investigate autoscaler lag + potential faster buffer scaling to avoid hitting divert thresholds.
maya_prodeng: Adding to roadmap: safe experiment gates and extra surge buffer for core regions. :memo:
